lessons.finding: The pipeline's most unanimous trades are its worst: 40% won, -0.28R, and every 5-domain name read as a filing-print reaction that had already gapped the entry (AMGN stopped -1.00R in 1 session, AMGN again -0.99R in 1 session, MRK 0.0R).
lessons.action: Treat 5-domain unanimity as a warning that the catalyst is already in the price; require a reversal-z pullback or a bid offset before sizing, and cap the score where the news prose describes an already-extended filing gap.

lessons.finding: Strongest cell in the run at 71% won and +0.30R: every winner sells a stale dated headline cluster into a low p/52wH, and the wide stop is what absorbs the 5d counter-bounce that supplies the entry (STLAM.MI x4, +0.61 to +0.84R).
lessons.action: Keep wide stops on shorts when the entry is a fade of a stale tariff/downgrade cluster at p/52wH below ~0.5; do not tighten just because the score looks low.

lessons.finding: 43% won at -0.21R, and the winners vs losers split cleanly on the stated reasoning: winners describe a flat 21d base at the high (DSFIR.AS '21d -0.1%', BBVA.MC '5d +1.5% no exhaustion'), losers describe being extended at 0.97-0.98 of the 52-week high with no pullback.
lessons.action: In the 3-4 domain bucket, only enter names whose reasoning describes a flat/contracting 21d at the high; demote names already extended at >=0.97 of the 52-week high.

lessons.finding: Coin-flip 50% hit rate but positive +0.18R, and the winners all have p/52wH below ~0.95 with a flat 21d while the full-stop losers are the ones bought at 0.98 of the high on vol-adj 2-3x momentum.
lessons.action: Require p/52wH below ~0.95 plus a non-extended 21d before accepting a wide-stop long; the 'great momentum but rich level' construction is what converts a wide stop into a full -1.0R.

lessons.finding: The pipeline's most-used entry band is also its worst at -0.06R over 23 closed, at an 88% fill rate that is no better than entering at the close - so the bid is buying no fill advantage and paying 0.26R per trade versus the close.
lessons.action: Stop using this band as the default entry; it is neither the close's fill reliability nor the deep bid's price advantage.

lessons.finding: 86% fill rate (statistically identical to the -1.5% to -0.25% band) with +0.20R over 23 closed - the pipeline's best combination of fill reliability and expectancy.
lessons.action: Default entries to the close unless there is a specific reason to bid lower; the fill rate does not improve by bidding down.

lessons.cell: entry below -1.5% (waiting for a better price)
lessons.finding: Only 44% of ideas at this entry ever traded, but the 7 that closed averaged +0.27R - the best closed-trade average in the fill record - and the winners are names already described as flat-21d bases, not falling knives.
lessons.action: Reserve deep bids for names whose reasoning already describes a flat 21d/str21 at the high; on trending names a deep bid just misses the move.

lessons.finding: Worst sector cell over the floor at 33% won and -0.12R, and the two IT names that paid (CRWD +1.28R, MU +0.56R) did so by expiring in the window rather than hitting a target, while the IT trades that hit a stop (QCOM, 8035.T) failed in one to six sessions.
lessons.action: On IT longs, prefer the expire-and-let-the-window-pay framing over a price target, and treat the first-session stop as the dominant failure mode to size against.
